title: Motion Intent
description: The boundary type (D-06). Everything upstream of this object may vary; everything downstream of it must be a function. Closed by default — 2020-12, and `additionalProperties: false` everywhere, following the practice recorded in the design notes. Exactly one field is left open, and it is named in `$defs.move.properties.quality`.

moves.description: The moves, in execution order. Moves sharing a `group` happen together; groups run in ascending order. The engine additionally requires, in code rather than here, that (a) groups are contiguous from zero, and (b) every move within a group has the same `duration_ms` — a JSON Schema cannot say either.

dof.description: The degree of freedom. ⚠️ These three names are ours, not the machine's — the control box documents no canonical axis correspondence, and the sign of every axis depends on the wiring. A name here is a label; it is not a motor number, and the engine never treats it as one.

target.description: Where to arrive, in the protocol's own units (counts). ⛔ The admissible range is deliberately NOT stated here. It is feedback-driven, not a constant that can be read off the protocol, and it belongs to the safety envelope that the host supplies at run time — not to the type. Holding the same number in two places is how the two come to disagree.

duration_ms.description: How long the move takes, in milliseconds.

group.description: Moves with the same group number run simultaneously. Groups run in ascending order, and must be contiguous from zero.

quality.description: ⛔ OPEN ON PURPOSE — the one field this type does not close. Its value type is undecided because the vocabulary that would fill it does not exist yet: the word-to-value mapping (08) is gated on D-12, which cannot be settled without the machine's response, and on D-02, which is gated on a question that is still open. Closing it now would make it impossible to write; but the engine does NOT read it — `engine/intent.py` builds its Move without this field, so a value written here changes nothing that runs. The boundary is therefore held from both sides: the schema allows the field, the code ignores it. This is where the collision between the type (D-06) and the vocabulary (08) is located — not erased.
